open_points.subject: Mapped node output disclosure class when mapped input is empty
open_points.text: A13 rule 6: "A mapped node over an empty list ... every output an empty list." and "its outputs are then lists ... each list of the highest class among its elements (A07)"; A07/M21 define class from received inputs or produced elements, but for zero elements no class is defined.
open_points.question: What disclosure_class must be assigned to each output value of a mapped node that runs over an empty list, so downstream disclosure checks and surface responses are deterministic?
options: Use `open` for every empty mapped output
Use the mapped node input's class
Use the proof-time reachable class for that output
open_points.default_guess: Use `open` for empty mapped outputs, by analogy with function output when no inputs.

open_points.subject: Service credential reference resolution at send time
open_points.text: A17 rule 2: "A credential is resolved only when a request to its service is built" but no outcome is specified if that resolution fails (missing reference, unreadable source, empty value).
open_points.question: If credential resolution fails while building a request, what exact node status/detail must be recorded, and is an EffectAttempt written for non-read operations?
open_points.default_guess: Treat as pre-send `operation_failed` with no EffectAttempt, because nothing was sent.

open_points.subject: Token list reload on changed but invalid configuration
open_points.text: A16 rule 2: "The kernel reads the token list again whenever the configuration file's content has changed ... before evaluating the next request." No behavior is defined when the changed file cannot be parsed/validated at that moment.
open_points.question: When live token reload detects changed configuration but the new token section is invalid, does the kernel keep old tokens, refuse all requests, or stop?
options: Keep last valid token set and continue
Refuse requests until config becomes valid
open_points.default_guess: Keep last valid token set and refuse only the reload attempt internally (continue serving).

open_points.subject: Grant revocation vs resume behavior for elements waiting `service_unreachable`
open_points.text: A14 rule 2 says resume "sends again ... every element waiting on `service_unreachable`"; A10 rule 5 says after revocation "an element already waiting then keeps waiting for an approval."
open_points.question: For an element currently waiting `service_unreachable` after a send authorized by a standing grant that is later revoked, should resume resend immediately, or must the element first transition to `owner_approval` and wait for explicit approval?
options: Revocation converts it to `owner_approval`; resume must not resend until approved
Behavior depends on whether an unused explicit approval exists
open_points.default_guess: Revocation should require approval before any further send (transition to `owner_approval`).

open_points.subject: Idempotency key fields that name file input ports
open_points.text: A08 rule 4 allows non-read idempotency key field names to be any input port names and defines key as SHA-256 of canonical JSON of those fields' values; A09 allows file input ports. Canonical JSON for file values is not defined.
open_points.question: Are file ports allowed in `idempotency_key_fields`, and if yes, what exact value representation is hashed for the EffectAttempt idempotency key?
options: Disallow file ports in idempotency key fields at proposal time
Allow file ports and hash file digest values
Allow file ports and hash raw bytes encoding
Allow but treat as key absent
open_points.default_guess: Disallow file ports in idempotency key fields for deterministic JSON-based hashing.
